chunks: And Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
"When the sun declines, the two times enter: al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr. Then when the sun sets, the two times enter: al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah."

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبُ: the evening prayer beginning at sunset
key_terms.الْوَقْتَانِ: the two times, meaning the paired prayer times entering together
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined from the zenith, referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurārah, the narrator transmitting this hadith

ai.seo_question: When do the times for Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ begin in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the commencement of the shared prayer times for the daily salat: the decline of the sun marks the start of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and sunset marks the start of Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ. It is significant in Shia fiqh for establishing the legal entry of these prayer times.
